title: Open WebUI image edit -- T1548 verified-account-only gate skips the global switch and per-user permission
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-59227 (GHSA-rqj7-6wrp-6g2g,
CVSS 4.3 MEDIUM), affecting Open WebUI from 0.8.11 before 0.10.0.

`POST /api/v1/images/edit` required only that the caller hold a
VERIFIED account -- it never checked either the deployment's global
image-edit feature switch (which an administrator may have turned off
entirely) or the per-user image-generation permission (which an
administrator may have denied to specific users or roles). Any
non-admin user who is merely verified -- the lowest bar for
authentication in the system -- can therefore invoke server-side
image editing using the administrator-configured provider credentials
(API keys for the image-editing backend), regardless of either
control the operator believed was gating the feature.

Detection logic flags a request to `/api/v1/images/edit` from a
non-admin, non-image-generation-permitted user -- the exact
permission-check gap this advisory describes; the endpoint's own
access model was "any verified account", not the operator's intended
"global switch AND per-user permission".

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (open-webui, via
GHSA and NVD, citing the exact fix commit and PR), fixed in 0.10.0.
